questions.q: What limiting belief held Jim Kwik back as a learner?
a: That he always had to work harder to learn
That intelligence could never be measured
That reading was a waste of time
That teachers could not be trusted
questions.why: The overview says his assumption that he had to work hard kept him back until he realized he needed to work smarter.

questions.q: What kind of music does Kwik recommend for studying?
a: Baroque music between 50 and 80 beats per minute
Electronic music with a fast, steady beat
Silence with occasional white noise
Classical symphonies at any tempo
questions.why: The first lesson says the author suggests Baroque music that runs between 50 and 80 beats per minute.

questions.q: How does Kwik suggest using smell to remember better?
a: Use the same essential oil while studying and at the exam
Burn a different candle for each subject
Avoid scents entirely so they cannot distract you
Spray perfume on your notes before reading
questions.why: He suggests using one scent during study sessions, then repeating it in the exam room.

Repeating a list aloud until it sticks
Drawing a diagram of every idea you read
Linking words into a made-up story
questions.why: You pick a place you know well, attach each part of the material to an object there, then mentally walk through the room.

questions.q: What does Kwik say subvocalizing does to your reading?
a: It limits your speed to how fast you can speak
It improves comprehension of difficult texts
It helps you remember names and dates
It should be practiced for ten minutes daily
questions.why: The third lesson says pronouncing each word in your head caps your reading and learning at speaking speed.
